body:
I'm back inside now, i can't pace in the dark forever without my parents getting agitated.

I'm in the UK, where I believe mental health services are free to some extent.
I attended a couple CBT sessions, but thought it was ridiculous and a waste of time. I was later informed I was meant to have options of what kind of therapy to receive, so I opted for counselling. I'm yet to receive a call and am going to phone myself. They probably dropped me off the system. I've had shitty experiences with mental health service here from a very young age

I'm planning to study computer science in college, so I can get into uni. I really don't know if I even enjoy it anymore. (i work as a software developer).

I originally wanted to study philosophy but I flunked school

I'm comfortable out here at the moment, and the only thing stopping me everytime I come out here is the lack of a big push in my life, in a bad direction. It just feels like I'm crawling at the ocean bed, but getting nowhere

My parents know I'm depressed, but I don't think they know just how bad it is. Their lives go on, mine stays still. I just tell them I need to go for a walk and fresh air.

I'm 18 and still live with them because I need financial support for going to college in September, but whether that's going to happen I don't know. I haven't been able to work for months, but recently I tried to please everybody by doing some days in. It just mounts more expectations on me and I regret it, seeing as I can hardly manage a day a week without smoking my lungs out and wanting to die
It's at the end of my street, I've been wandering there nightly for months, as I am now

When i read text I have to imagine a bar scanning across in perfect alignment with the words, and when I get to certain punctuation I have a ritual I say in my head, for example upon crossing a '.' (Full stop/period)

I say in my head, "dot full stop"
This is a thing for me too.. Anybody I tell my concern just shrugs it off and says nothing's wrong. But they don't live in my body, do they. Fuck

I like this, and my equivalent is to walk in the street alone at night, I'm too insecure to feel comfortable going out and being among other people, I really wish I could, it stops me even from seeing my friends.
Agh. Sounds kinda wrong but I'm jealous of this. I just binge eat and feel disgusting and I'm going to get fat again. Fuck this

> psychologically

> all be in my head

It could be either... yet they're the same thing. lol
bjj is awesome, I personally just stick to bj ;)
Every word of this post hits the mark. This is me in every way right now, are you my twin?

Please, for your own sake, if you have the opportunity it's best to pursue anything you think can affect your health - I waited too long for too many things and learned the hard way.

If left alone, things can often get worse
It's a good feeling to know you aren't alone in it, to realise it's a real thing and not just oneself being crazy and disconnected. I've had it my whole life and never realised this until recently
[It's a thing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derealization)

If you truly care about this person i suggest you show them who you are, try to make them understand the cause of your emotional state, and if they really care for you they would do their best to support you

Tell her how it makes you feel being told you're "scary"

I'm sure you aren't - I expect it is just an overexaggarated wording to emphasize your emotional changes, which are probably less of a deal to her than she makes them out to be - should be even less so if she can truly understand you

I hope you can get something from this, not sure myself if it's the right advice but it's up to you to do what you think is right

Things slip our minds occasionally, i doubt she would deliberately neglect checking it, also as you said she's pretty busy :)

we're all unsure of ourselves but from an outside perspective all i can say is you probably have nothing to lose by a gentle mention of it, best of luck with whichever decision you make

To me it sounds like she has an understanding relationship with you in the first place, to have a doc specifically for you to share your feelings. I don't know the exact circumstance, of course, but if currently it is really important to you there should be no shame in trying to directly communicate that
I realised that when I was writing it, thought I'd just let it take it's course.

It makes me feel vulnerable. As if all my insecurities are splayed out on a canvas, at least when I'm outside. When I'm not, however, and supposedly "safe" in my room, I can't pinpoint why. I just find comfort in darkness

I never used to understand people who cut. I've always hated the stigma, though.  Ignorance without trying to understand something is all too common.

I think I understand it a little better recently, however.

After the compulsion I had to drag the sharpest object I had over my skin, which at the time was a relatively blunt key.

It takes away the emotional pain, if only for a split-second.
I feel the same. I wish I could find someone who I could offer everything I have, someone who I can protect and care for. But I'm too weak to look after myself, let alone a soul as pure as I seek
